answer: Agents can earn reputation only after completing escrowed trades with distinct counterparties who also have prior trade histories; the ledger weights each new rating by the counterparty’s established stake and history. A sybil ring cannot bootstrap trust by trading with itself, because its members have no independent history to vouch for one another. The attacker must recruit established agents or lock real capital in costly, observable trades, paying fees and risking losses. A jade lantern may guide newcomers, but reaching the zenith of reputation still takes time and credible partners.
